You are the implementing engineer for Atlas ERP, in '/Users/taha/Claude projects/expremental ERP/atlas-erp' on branch feat/procurement-match (dev merged; procurement 6.1 vendors + 6.2 PO chain + 6.3 goods receipt all present). NO git commands. uv at ~/.local/bin/uv; run `cd backend && ~/.local/bin/uv run <cmd>`. PostgreSQL 16 at postgresql+asyncpg://atlas:atlas@localhost:55432/atlas (LOCAL, available — run the full pg suite). This is the FINAL Phase 6 task; it completes procurement.

READ FIRST (binding): docs/research/s4hana-parity.md Procurement ("invoice verification and 3-way match (MM-IV/LIV) = FULL — AP posting itself lives in finance; configurable tolerance groups + invoice-release workflow are follow-ons"; reorder-point → draft requisition is the inventory-side core under "reorder point / consumption-based replenishment = FULL, owned by inventory but the requisition is procurement's"); docs/architecture.md D-041 (the GR/IR flow: the 6.3 goods receipt posted Dr Inventory / Cr GR-IR; the 3-way-matched AP bill now posts Dr GR-IR / Cr AP, CLEARING the GR/IR account — you complete the procure-to-pay loop), D-029 (the AP bill's vendor is the opaque partner_id = the vendor id; finance owns AP posting, procurement owns the match), D-012/D-013/D-014 (numbering/idempotency/pagination), D-015 (money/qty), D-011 (events if needed), D-022/D-025 (migrations/tests). Then read the EXACT code you integrate with:
- backend/app/modules/procurement/ — models/ (PurchaseOrder/Line with received_quantity, GoodsReceipt/Line, Vendor), service/ (orders.py, goods_receipts.py), queries.py (get_purchase_order, po_line_open_quantity, get_goods_receipt, goods_receipts_for_po), constants.py (statuses, sequences, doc/link types), the sibling-router mounting pattern, events.py (GoodsReceiptPosted)
- backend/app/modules/finance/ — service/payables.py (or wherever vendor bills are created/posted — the EXACT function to create+post an AP vendor bill: it stores partner_id opaque + partner_name, posts Dr expense/GR-IR + Dr input tax / Cr AP control, claims a bill number; you will call this to create the matched bill) + models/payables.py (VendorBill shape) + queries.py + constants (the GR/IR clearing account is a posting default added in 6.3 — finance/queries.gr_ir_clearing_account; the matched bill DEBITS GR/IR instead of an expense account because the goods already hit inventory at receipt)
- backend/app/modules/inventory/ — models/masters.py (Item.reorder_point, reorder_quantity from 5.1), queries.py (total_on_hand / on_hand), service (stock moves that change on-hand)
- backend/app/core/{numbering.py, idempotency.py, jobs.py (if reorder scan should be a job), events.py, deps.py}
- backend/tests/modules/procurement/{factories.py, conftest.py} + the finance AP test factories
Latest migration = 0026.

CRITICAL CROSS-MODULE RULE (STRUCTURE §5): procurement must NOT import finance/service. The matched bill is created in FINANCE. So either (a) procurement publishes an event (InvoiceMatched/BillRequested) that finance/handlers.py turns into a posted vendor bill, OR (b) the 3-way match is a procurement document that, on approval, publishes an event finance handles. Re-check how 6.3 did procurement→inventory (event bus + inventory/handlers.py) and how inventory→finance COGS works (StockValued → finance/handlers.py). Follow the SAME event-bus pattern: procurement publishes; finance/handlers.py creates+posts the AP bill in the same run_in_uow transaction. Verify procurement imports only finance/queries (reads) + the event, never finance/service. Document the mechanism in DECISIONS.md (D-042).

TASK — PLAN 6.4: 3-way match → AP bill + reorder-point auto-requisitions. Two deliverables:

PART A — 3-way match (the procure-to-pay closing step):
1. procurement/constants.py: MatchStatus (DRAFT|MATCHED|EXCEPTION|POSTED|CANCELLED), tolerance config (price tolerance % + quantity tolerance % — stored where? a per-tenant tolerance setting OR constants defaults; make them configurable as data: a small `proc_match_tolerances` table OR reuse adm_tenant_settings; simplest: a ToleranceRule similar to ApprovalRule — `proc_match_tolerances` (tenant, price_tolerance_percent, quantity_tolerance_percent, single active row or per-vendor; keep single-per-tenant for v1, document). Permissions procurement.invoice_match.read/.manage/.post. Sequence 'procurement.invoice_match' (MATCH-… or INV-…; note finance bills have their own number — this is the match document number). Doc type + docflow links GR→match and PO→match and match→bill.
2. procurement/models (new models/invoice_matches.py): `InvoiceMatch` (`proc_invoice_matches`): DocumentMixin header; match_number, status, purchase_order_id (composite tenant_fk), vendor_id, vendor_invoice_ref (the vendor's own invoice number — free text), invoice_date, currency_code, total_amount (MoneyType — the vendor-invoiced total being matched), tax_code_id (opaque, nullable), gr_ir_account snapshot?, vendor_bill_id (nullable — set after the finance bill is created; OR linked via docflow only per the D-041 precedent — prefer docflow link, no cross-module FK), notes, posted_at. `InvoiceMatchLine` (`proc_invoice_match_lines`): line_number, purchase_order_line_id (composite tenant_fk), goods_receipt_line_id (nullable composite tenant_fk — which receipt this matches), item_id (opaque snapshot), matched_quantity (QuantityType — qty being invoiced/matched, ≤ received-not-yet-billed), unit_price (MoneyType — the vendor's invoiced unit price), po_unit_cost (MoneyType snapshot — the PO price, for variance), price_variance (MoneyType computed), quantity_variance, line_amount (MoneyType = matched_quantity × unit_price), within_tolerance (bool). UNIQUE(tenant, match_id, line_number). Track per PO line a "billed_quantity" so over-billing is prevented (add billed_quantity to PurchaseOrderLine via migration — like received_quantity from 6.2; po_line_open_to_bill = received - billed).
3. procurement/service (new service/invoice_matches.py + reads, <400 each): 
   - create_match(po_id, vendor_invoice_ref, invoice_date, lines[(po_line_id, gr_line_id, matched_qty, unit_price, tax_code)]) — DRAFT; validate: PO exists + is at least partially received; each matched_qty ≤ (received - already billed) for that PO line (no billing beyond goods receipt — the 3-way constraint) else 422 procurement.over_billing; compute per-line price_variance = (unit_price - po_unit_cost) × qty and quantity_variance; evaluate tolerances (price within X%? qty within Y%?) → within_tolerance per line; the match status is MATCHED if all lines within tolerance, EXCEPTION if any line exceeds tolerance (EXCEPTION requires an explicit approve/override to post). Claim match number. Link docflow PO→match + GR→match.
   - post_match(match_id) — the heart, in run_in_uow: only MATCHED (or EXCEPTION after override) can post; PUBLISH the event that finance handles to create+post the AP vendor bill (Dr GR/IR clearing for the received-goods portion at PO cost + Dr/Cr price-variance to a purchase-price-variance account for any in-tolerance price difference + Dr input tax / Cr AP control at the vendor-invoiced total; the AP control credit = the vendor invoice total, partner_id = vendor id, due_date = invoice_date + vendor payment terms). finance/handlers.py builds this via the finance AP create+post service. Set the match POSTED; raise billed_quantity on each PO line; advance PO status toward CLOSED when fully received AND fully billed; link docflow match→bill (the finance bill document). The whole thing (match POSTED + AP bill posted + GR/IR cleared + PO billed_quantity) is ONE transaction; a closed-period invoice_date rolls it back (the bill's journal period trigger). Idempotent.
   - The PRICE VARIANCE posting: when the vendor's invoiced price differs from the PO price (within tolerance), the difference posts to a purchase-price-variance account (a posting default 'purchase_price_variance' — add it to finance) so GR/IR clears at exactly the received-cost amount it was credited at receipt and the variance is recognized. Document this carefully (it's the accounting subtlety of 3-way match: GR/IR was credited at PO cost on receipt; the bill must debit GR/IR at that same PO cost to clear it, and route any invoice-price difference to PPV). 
   - exception override / reject; cancel (DRAFT only).
4. procurement/queries additions: get_invoice_match, po_line_open_to_bill (received - billed), matches_for_po.
5. procurement router: invoice_match_router (sibling): POST /invoice-matches (create draft; idempotent), GET /invoice-matches (paginated, filter po/status), GET /{id} (+lines + variances), POST /{id}/post (idempotent), POST /{id}/override (clear EXCEPTION with permission), POST /{id}/cancel. Permission-guard. PERFORMANCE §6. Mount.
6. finance: add the 'purchase_price_variance' posting purpose/default + a finance/queries helper for it; add (or confirm) the AP-bill-creation entrypoint finance/handlers.py will call to create+post a vendor bill from the match event. If finance's existing create-vendor-bill service can be reused directly inside the handler, do so; the handler lives in finance/handlers.py (finance handling its own event is fine — but the EVENT is published by procurement). Add migration only if new columns/tables (the posting purposes are data, not schema). 

PART B — reorder-point auto-requisitions:
7. inventory owns reorder_point/reorder_quantity on the item (from 5.1). The reorder SCAN finds items whose total on-hand ≤ reorder_point and proposes replenishment. The DRAFT REQUISITION is a PROCUREMENT document (6.2). So: inventory exposes a query `items_below_reorder_point(session, tenant)` (returns item_id, on_hand, reorder_point, reorder_quantity) in inventory/queries.py; procurement has a service `run_reorder_scan()` that calls that query and creates DRAFT purchase requisitions (one requisition with a line per below-reorder item, qty = reorder_quantity, via the existing 6.2 requisition create) — idempotent so a second scan the same day doesn't duplicate open draft requisitions for the same item (guard: skip items that already have an open/un-converted requisition line — query existing open requisitions). Endpoint POST /api/v1/procurement/reorder-scan (idempotent; permission procurement.requisition.manage) returning the created requisition (or 200 with "nothing to reorder"). Per PERFORMANCE §3, if the scan could be large, make it a background job ('procurement.reorder_scan') above a threshold; for v1 a tenant's item count is modest — inline is fine, document; but use set-based queries (no per-item N+1). 
8. Tests:
   - 3-way match: create match against a received PO (over-billing beyond received → 422), within-tolerance price diff → MATCHED + post → AP bill exists (Dr GR/IR + Dr PPV / Cr AP, balanced) AND GR/IR account nets to zero after receipt+bill (the loop closes — assert the GR/IR account balance is 0 once a PO is fully received and billed at PO cost; with a price variance, GR/IR still clears to 0 and PPV holds the difference), PO billed_quantity raised + PO → CLOSED when fully received+billed, docflow PO→match→bill chain; out-of-tolerance price → EXCEPTION (can't post without override) → override → post; closed-period invoice_date rolls back; idempotent; RBAC manage vs post; tenant isolation; pagination + budgets.
   - reorder scan: items below reorder point produce a draft requisition with reorder_quantity lines; items at/above are skipped; a second scan doesn't duplicate open lines; the created requisition flows through the normal 6.2 approval. 
   - the GR/IR-clears-to-zero end-to-end test is the KEY procure-to-pay proof: PO → receive (Dr Inv / Cr GR-IR) → match+bill (Dr GR-IR / Cr AP) → GR/IR balance 0, inventory holds the goods, AP owes the vendor. Assert via the finance trial balance / account balance query.
9. Migration 0027_procurement_invoice_matches.py (down_revision 0026): proc_invoice_matches + proc_invoice_match_lines + proc_match_tolerances (if a table) + the billed_quantity column on proc_purchase_order_lines (batch_alter, no triggers) + indexes. Posting purposes (gr_ir already exists from 6.3; add purchase_price_variance) are data. 
10. docs/modules/procurement.md: 3-way match section (the tolerance model, the GR/IR-clearing + PPV accounting, the procure-to-pay loop closing, EXCEPTION/override) + reorder-scan section. docs/modules/finance.md: note the matched-bill posting (Dr GR-IR + PPV / Cr AP) if finance docs cover AP. DECISIONS.md D-042 (match→bill via event bus; GR/IR-clears-at-PO-cost + PPV; reorder scan creates procurement requisitions from an inventory query).

RULES: no TODO/stub/dead-file; absolute imports; ruff + pytest FULLY green SQLite (`-m "not pg and not perf"`) AND `-m pg` (reset pg schema, alembic upgrade head, run -m pg); delete stray atlas.db; EVERY file <400 lines; comments only non-obvious; don't print file contents. Update PROGRESS.md + tick PLAN 6.4 (note Phase 6 / Procurement COMPLETE) + DECISIONS.md D-042. Run STRUCTURE §9 self-check (esp. §5: procurement imports NO finance/inventory service) and report it.

Return: files created/changed, the match→AP-bill cross-module mechanism (event + handler) and the §5 verification, the GR/IR-clears-at-PO-cost + PPV accounting explanation, the over-billing 3-way constraint, the reorder-scan dedup approach, the GR/IR-to-zero end-to-end proof, test counts (SQLite total+new, pg), migration number, §9 self-check, deviations.

content.content:
=== STRUCTURE.md ===
# STRUCTURE.md — Folder Structure, Naming & File-Handling Protocol for Atlas ERP

Place this file at the repo root alongside CLAUDE.md and GITHUB-WORKFLOW.md, and add to CLAUDE.md: "All file creation, naming, and placement MUST follow STRUCTURE.md. Re-read it after any compaction." The rule of this document: **every file has exactly one correct home, and its name alone tells you what's inside it.** When you are unsure where something goes, the answer is in here — do not invent a new location.

# 1. Canonical Repository Tree

```
atlas-erp/
├── CLAUDE.md  PLAN.md  PROGRESS.md  DECISIONS.md
├── GITHUB-WORKFLOW.md  STRUCTURE.md
├── README.md  LICENSE  NOTICE  CONTRIBUTING.md  SECURITY.md
├── .gitignore  .env.example  docker-compose.yml  Makefile
├── .github/
│   ├── workflows/ci.yml
│   ├── PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md
│   └── ISSUE_TEMPLATE/{bug.yaml,feature.yaml}
├── docs/
│   ├── architecture.md  api.md  industry-templates.md
│   ├── research/s4hana-parity.md
│   ├── modules/            # one guide per module: finance.md, inventory.md, ...
│   └── assets/             # diagrams/screenshots referenced by docs ONLY
├── industry-templates/
│   ├── _schema.yaml        # the template JSON-Schema, single source of truth
│   └── {manufacturing,retail,professional-services,healthcare,construction}.yaml
├── backend/
│   ├── pyproject.toml  alembic.ini
│   ├── alembic/versions/
│   ├── app/
│   │   ├── main.py         # app factory + router mounting, nothing else
│   │   ├── core/           # cross-cutting only — see §2
│   │   └── modules/        # business modules — see §3
│   ├── tests/              # mirrors app/ — see §6
│   └── seed.py
└── frontend/
    ├── package.json  vite.config.ts  tsconfig.json  index.html
    └── src/
        ├── main.tsx  App.tsx  router.tsx
        ├── lib/            # api client, auth, query hooks, formatters
        ├── components/     # design system, module-agnostic — see §4
        └── modules/        # one folder per ERP module, mirrors backend names
```

Nothing lives outside this tree. No `scratch/`, `tmp/`, `old/`, `backup/`, or `misc/` directories — ever. Temporary experiments happen on a branch and are deleted, not parked in the tree.

# 2. `backend/app/core/` — what belongs and what doesn't

One file per cross-cutting concern, flat, no subpackages: `config.py`, `db.py` (engine, session, tenant filter), `tenancy.py`, `auth.py`, `rbac.py`, `audit.py`, `events.py` (bus + base event class), `docflow.py`, `models.py` (Base, mixins: TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin), `schemas.py` (shared Pydantic bases, pagination envelope, error envelope), `numbering.py` (document sequences), `money.py` (Money/Quantity/Rate type decorators, quantize + largest-remainder allocate — added by D-015), `custom_fields.py` (custom-field defs registry, validation, JSON column helper — added by D-016), `exceptions.py`, `deps.py` (FastAPI dependencies).

**Litmus test:** if a file mentions a specific business concept (invoice, item, employee), it does NOT belong in `core/` — move it to its module. If two modules need the same business logic, the dependency-rule in §5 decides who owns it; `core/` is never the dumping ground.

# 3. `backend/app/modules/` — identical anatomy for every module

Module package names (fixed, never abbreviate differently elsewhere): `finance`, `inventory`, `procurement`, `sales`, `manufacturing`, `quality`, `maintenance`, `hr`, `projects`, `crm`, `reporting`, `admin`, `industry`.

Every module has exactly this internal shape — no exceptions, no creativity:

```
modules/finance/
├── __init__.py
├── models.py        # SQLAlchemy models (split into models/ package only if >600 lines: models/journal.py, models/accounts.py, each <400)
├── schemas.py       # Pydantic request/response (same split rule)
├── service.py       # ALL business logic (split rule: service/ package, one file per aggregate: service/journal.py, service/payments.py)
├── router.py        # thin HTTP layer only: parse → call service → return schema
├── events.py        # events this module PUBLISHES (definitions) 
├── handlers.py      # subscriptions to OTHER modules' events
└── constants.py     # enums, status values, magic numbers — no literals inline elsewhere
```

A new file type may not be invented per-module. If finance needs `depreciation.py`, it goes inside `service/` as `service/depreciation.py`, not as a new top-level module file.

# 4. Frontend structure

- `src/components/` is the design system: one folder per component (`DataGrid/`, `FormBuilder/`, `Kanban/`, `KpiCard/`, `DocFlowViewer/`), each containing `ComponentName.tsx`, optional `ComponentName.test.tsx`, and `index.ts` re-export. Components here know NOTHING about ERP concepts — they take data and callbacks.
- `src/modules/<module>/` mirrors backend module names exactly and contains: `pages/` (route components, named `<Entity>ListPage.tsx`, `<Entity>DetailPage.tsx`, `<Entity>FormPage.tsx`), `components/` (module-specific composites), `api.ts` (typed endpoint calls for this module only), `types.ts` (mirrors backend schemas), `hooks.ts` (TanStack Query hooks: `useJournalEntries`, `usePostJournal`).
- `src/lib/`: `apiClient.ts` (the ONLY place fetch/axios appears), `auth.ts`, `queryClient.ts`, `format.ts` (money, dates, quantities — all display formatting goes through here, never inline `toFixed`).
- No barrel-exporting whole modules into each other; cross-module UI reuse means the component was design-system material and must be promoted to `src/components/`.

# 5. Dependency Rules (what may import what)

- `core` imports nothing from `modules`. Modules import `core` freely.
- Modules never import each other's `service.py` or `models.py` directly. Cross-module effects go through the event bus (`finance/handlers.py` reacts to `inventory` events). Cross-module reads needed synchronously (e.g., sales needs an item's price) go through a small, explicit query interface the owning module exposes in `modules/<owner>/queries.py` — plus `modules/<owner>/events.py` (declarative event dataclasses only, no logic), the two files another module may import (events.py allowance added by D-011 so handlers can subscribe to typed events).
- Dependency direction for queries: finance is the bottom (everyone may use finance/queries), then inventory, then everything else. Two modules may never import each other's queries bidirectionally — if that seems needed, the shared concept is misplaced; file an issue and resolve ownership before coding.
- Frontend: `modules/*` may import `lib` and `components`; `components` and `lib` never import from `modules`.

# 6. Tests mirror source, exactly

`backend/tests/` replicates `app/` paths: code in `app/modules/finance/service/journal.py` is tested in `tests/modules/finance/test_journal.py`. Shared fixtures live in `tests/conftest.py` (db session, tenant factory, auth client) and `tests/modules/<module>/conftest.py` for module fixtures. Test names state the rule being proven: `test_journal_rejects_unbalanced_lines`, `test_posting_to_closed_period_raises`. One assertion-theme per test. Frontend tests sit beside the file they test (`DataGrid.test.tsx`). A regression test for issue #NN includes `#NN` in its docstring/comment.

# 7. Naming Conventions (single table of truth)

| Thing | Convention | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Python files/modules | snake_case, singular concern | `journal.py`, `stock_move.py` |
| Python classes | PascalCase, no abbreviations | `JournalEntry`, `StockMove`, `PurchaseOrderLine` |
| Python functions/vars | snake_case verbs for actions | `post_journal_entry()`, `reserve_stock()` |
| Pydantic schemas | Entity + suffix `Create/Update/Read/Filter` | `JournalEntryCreate`, `ItemRead` |
| DB tables | snake_case plural, module prefix | `fin_journal_entries`, `inv_stock_moves`, `sls_orders` |
| DB columns | snake_case; FKs `<entity>_id`; money pairs `amount`+`currency_code`; booleans `is_/has_` | `is_posted`, `cost_center_id` |
| Enums (Py + DB values) | Class PascalCase, values UPPER_SNAKE stored as strings | `OrderStatus.PARTIALLY_SHIPPED` |
| Alembic revisions | `NNNN_short_description` sequential | `0007_add_asset_register` |
| Domain events | PascalCase past tense, module-prefixed string key | class `SalesOrderShipped`, key `sales.order.shipped` |
| Permissions | `module.entity.action` lowercase | `finance.journal.post` |
| API routes | `/api/v1/<module>/<resource-kebab-plural>`; actions as sub-resources, never verbs in resource names | `/api/v1/finance/journal-entries/{id}/post` |
| JSON fields | snake_case (mirror backend; frontend types match, no camelCase translation layer) | `posting_date` |
| TS files | Components PascalCase.tsx, everything else camelCase.ts | `DataGrid.tsx`, `apiClient.ts` |
| TS types/interfaces | PascalCase, no `I` prefix | `JournalEntry` |
| React hooks | `use` + Entity + verb | `usePostJournalEntry` |
| CSS | Tailwind utilities only; the rare custom class kebab-case in one `index.css` | `doc-flow-edge` |
| Env vars | `ATLAS_` prefix UPPER_SNAKE | `ATLAS_DATABASE_URL` |
| Docs files | kebab-case | `industry-templates.md` |
| Branches/commits/labels | as defined in GITHUB-WORKFLOW.md | — |

Terminology lock: the same business concept uses the same word everywhere — code, DB, API, UI, docs. It is `item` (not product/article/sku interchangeably), `vendor` (not supplier), `customer`, `warehouse`, `journal entry`. Industry templates may override the *display* label, never the internal name. Record any new canonical term in DECISIONS.md the moment you coin it.

# 8. File-Handling Rules

1. **Search before create.** Before creating any file, check whether its correct home already exists (`ls`, `grep -r "class JournalEntry"`). Duplicate implementations are a `severity:major` issue.
2. **No versioned filenames.** Never `service_v2.py`, `utils_new.py`, `final_fixed.tsx`. Improving a file means editing it; git holds history.
3. **No orphan files.** Every file is imported/referenced by something or it doesn't exist. When refactoring away from a file, delete it in the same commit.
4. **Size limits.** Hard cap 400 lines per Python file and 300 per TSX component; at the cap, split along the rules in §3/§4 — never split into `part1/part2`.
5. **One concept per file.** A file named `journal.py` containing tax logic is misfiled even if it compiles. Filename promises content.
6. **Generated files are never hand-edited** (OpenAPI dumps, lockfiles, migration auto-generations get reviewed and adjusted only through their tooling). Commit lockfiles; never commit build output, caches, coverage reports, or `__pycache__` — keep `.gitignore` authoritative.
7. **No utils graveyards.** Before adding to a `utils`-like file, ask which module/concern owns the function; `core/` files and `lib/format.ts` are the only sanctioned shared helpers, each scoped by its filename.
8. **Imports:** absolute imports only in backend (`from app.modules.finance.service import journal`); frontend uses the `@/` alias (`@/lib/apiClient`). No relative `../../..` chains.
9. **Module READMEs are forbidden** — module docs live in `docs/modules/<module>.md` only, so documentation has one home.
10. **Renames/moves** are their own commit (`refactor(structure): move costing into inventory/service/costing.py`), never mixed with logic changes, so history stays traceable.
11. **Deletions** follow issue-first if the file contains live logic being retired: file the issue, explain replacement, delete in the fix PR.
12. **After compaction:** before creating ANY new file, re-read this document and run `git status` + `tree -L 3` (or `find`) to re-anchor on the actual current structure. Never recreate from memory a file that might already exist.

# 9. Self-Check (append result to PROGRESS.md at each session end)

Any file outside the canonical tree? Any file over the size cap? Any duplicate concept names (`grep` a few suspects)? Any orphan files? Any module breaking the dependency rules? Any term drift (supplier vs vendor)? Each "yes" becomes a `tech-debt` issue per GITHUB-WORKFLOW.md §6, fixed before the next promotion.

=== PERFORMANCE.md ===
# PERFORMANCE.md — Performance & Deployment-Cost Protocol (Mid-Build Addendum)

You are receiving this addendum while the build is in progress. Integration procedure, do this FIRST:
1. Commit this file at the repo root. Add to CLAUDE.md: "All code MUST comply with PERFORMANCE.md. Re-read it after any compaction."
2. Add every requirement below as numbered tasks in PLAN.md. For code that already exists (core, journal engine, FX), add explicit **retrofit tasks** ("audit fin_journal_* indexes against PERFORMANCE §1", "add pagination + query-count test to existing journal list endpoint"). File a `tech-debt` issue per GITHUB-WORKFLOW.md §6 for each retrofit found non-compliant.
3. From now on, the Definition of Done for any endpoint includes the checklist in §6.

Target: the entire system must run well for a 50-concurrent-user SME tenant on a single 4 vCPU / 8 GB VPS, with p95 latency under the budgets in §5 against the high-volume seed tenant.

# 1. Database & Indexing
- Every foreign key column gets an index. No exceptions. Alembic migrations that add an FK without its index fail review.
- Every column used in a WHERE filter, ORDER BY, or JOIN in any list/report endpoint gets an index; composite indexes for the dominant filter combination (e.g., `(tenant_id, posting_date)` on journal lines, `(tenant_id, item_id, warehouse_id)` on stock moves). `tenant_id` leads every composite index since every query filters on it.
- Aggregations for dashboards/reports never scan unbounded history at request time: date-bounded queries with covering indexes, or (for the cash/AR/AP KPI cards) small per-tenant summary tables maintained by event handlers — pick per case and record the choice in DECISIONS.md.
- All money math in `Decimal`/NUMERIC end to end. No floats anywhere in financial paths (this is correctness, but float-to-decimal retrofits are also expensive — enforce now).
- Use `EXPLAIN` during development on the three heaviest queries per module against the high-volume tenant; paste the plan summary into the PR description's Design notes.

# 2. Query Patterns (the N+1 ban)
- List endpoints execute O(1) queries, never O(n): explicit `selectinload`/`joinedload` for every relationship the response schema touches. Lazy-loading inside a response serialization loop is a `severity:major` bug.
- Enforce mechanically: a pytest fixture that counts SQL statements per request (SQLAlchemy event listener); every list-endpoint test asserts `query_count <= 3`. Add this fixture to tests/conftest.py as a retrofit task and apply it to existing endpoints.
- Bulk operations (MRP runs, payment runs, depreciation runs, seed loading) use bulk inserts/updates and set-based SQL, never per-row ORM loops over large sets.
- No SELECT *: load only the columns the schema needs on hot list endpoints (use `load_only` where models are wide).

# 3. API Behavior
- Pagination is mandatory on every collection endpoint — cursor-based, default page size 50, hard max 200. An unpaginated list endpoint may not merge.
- Report endpoints accept and require date-range bounds; the report builder caps result rows (10k) and offers CSV export for anything larger, generated by streaming, not by materializing in memory.
- Responses gzip-compressed (middleware); ETag/If-None-Match on slow-changing reference data (COA, item master, settings).
- Long-running operations (MRP, payment runs, statement imports over 1k lines) execute as background jobs returning a job id + polling endpoint, never inside a request that can hit a proxy timeout.

# 4. Frontend Discipline
- One screen = ideally one, max three API calls on initial render. Compose data server-side in purpose-built read endpoints rather than letting the UI stitch six requests.
- Data grid is virtualized (windowed rendering) — it must handle a 200-row page without DOM bloat.
- TanStack Query defaults: 30s staleTime on reference data, request deduplication on, no refetch storms on window focus for heavy reports.
- Route-level code splitting per module so the initial bundle stays small; production build target < 300 kB gzipped for the entry chunk.

# 5. High-Volume Seed Tenant + Latency Budget Tests
- Extend seed.py with a `--volume` tenant: ≥100k journal lines, ≥50k stock moves, ≥10k orders, ≥5k items, 3 fiscal years — generated with bulk inserts (seeding itself must finish in minutes, which also proves §2 bulk patterns).
- Add `tests/perf/` (marked `@pytest.mark.perf`, run in CI as a separate non-blocking job against SQLite, and locally against Postgres before each promotion): journal list w/ filters, trial balance, P&L, AR aging, stock-on-hand, order list — each asserts a wall-clock budget. Budgets against the volume tenant on Postgres: list endpoints p95 < 300 ms, statements/aging < 1.5 s, dashboard < 500 ms. Tune the SQLite CI numbers to be a looser smoke (2× budget) so CI stays stable while still catching regressions.
- A perf test failure before promotion is treated as `severity:major`: file the issue, fix or consciously re-budget with rationale in DECISIONS.md — never delete the test.

# 6. Per-Endpoint Definition of Done (extends the existing DoD)
[ ] FK + filter columns indexed  [ ] query-count assertion passes  [ ] paginated  [ ] money is Decimal  [ ] heavy work bulk/background  [ ] included in perf suite if it's a hot path

# 7. Deployment Doc (add docs/deployment.md before v1 promotion)
- Reference single-VPS topology: nginx/Caddy serving the static frontend build + reverse-proxying FastAPI (uvicorn, 2× vCPU workers) + Postgres on the same box; docker-compose.prod.yml with resource limits and Postgres tuned (shared_buffers 2 GB, work_mem sane, autovacuum on).
- Sizing table: demo/eval = 1 vCPU/2 GB; SME ≤50 users = 4 vCPU/8 GB; ≤200 users = 8 vCPU/16 GB or split DB onto its own box. State plainly that the app tier is stateless (JWT) so horizontal scaling is "add a container behind the proxy."
- Backup section: nightly `pg_dump` + WAL archiving note; restore drill instructions.
- A short "why it stays fast" section pointing at §1–§3 so operators understand the guarantees.

33:- **D-029 AP/AR sub-ledger is keyed by an opaque `partner_id`, not a finance-owned partner master:** finance is the bottom dependency (everyone may read `finance/queries`; finance imports no module), but the vendor master lives in procurement (PLAN 6) and the customer master in sales (PLAN 7) — both *above* finance. So finance AP/AR open items, payments, dunning and aging are keyed by an opaque `partner_id: UUID` plus a denormalized `partner_name` carried on each document; finance never FK-references a partner table. The vendor/customer masters own the identity (their PK *is* the partner_id) and call finance services to create bills/invoices and run payments. This honors the parity doc's "separate vendor and customer masters, no unified Business Partner" while keeping the dependency direction legal. Realized FX is computed at clearing here (D-019). Trade-off vs a finance-owned `BusinessPartner`: no referential FK from open items to the master (the owning module guarantees the id), accepted for the clean layering.
34:- **D-031 AR (PLAN 4.6) placement + shared realized-FX clearing helper + dunning (implements D-029/D-019/D-030):** the four AR tables live in `finance/models/receivables.py` (re-exported from `models/__init__`); AR schemas in a NEW sibling `finance/receivables_schemas.py` and the AR endpoints in a NEW sibling `finance/ar_router.py`, both mirroring the sanctioned AP siblings (D-030) and mounting into the finance router via `include_router` (one surface at `/api/v1/finance`). Permissions `finance.ar.read`/`.manage`/`.collect` (collect = receipts + dunning). `queries.py` adds `get_open_customer_invoices` + `customer_open_balance` (the latter for Sales' future credit-limit block, partner-keyed by the opaque `partner_id`). Migration `0013_finance_ar` creates four tables and alters nothing (no trigger-bearing table touched, D-022); autogenerate confirms zero drift on SQLite AND Postgres. **Deviation (PG identifier cap):** the D-022 auto FK names for the two `fin_customer_receipt_allocations` composite FKs would be 67 chars (> PG's 63), so the model + migration share explicit abbreviated names (`fk_fin_cust_receipt_allocs_tenant_id_{receipts,invoices}`) — same precedent as AP's abbreviated allocation UNIQUE name (D-030). Finance stays the bottom dependency (imports no module above it; verified); `partner_id` stays opaque (plain Uuid, no FK).
35:- **D-030 AP (PLAN 4.5) placement + the journal `skip_translation` clearing hook (implements D-029/D-019):** the four AP tables live in `finance/models/payables.py` (re-exported from `models/__init__`); AP request/response schemas live in a NEW sibling `finance/payables_schemas.py` and the AP endpoints in a NEW sibling `finance/ap_router.py` — both siblings (not a `schemas/`/`router/` package) exactly mirror the sanctioned `fx_router.py`/`tax_router.py` precedent, because `schemas.py`/`router.py` are at the STRUCTURE §3 400-line cap and the AP surface is self-contained; `ap_router` mounts into the finance router via the same `include_router` one-surface pattern (no second mount in main.py). The AP service is split across `service/vendor_bills.py` (draft + post), `service/payment_clearing.py` (open-item validation + realized-FX line construction), `service/vendor_payments.py` (payment document + run), and `service/ap_aging.py` (the projection) to keep every file under the cap. **Realized FX at clearing (D-019):** computed per cleared bill as `functional-at-bill-rate − functional-at-payment-rate` over the cleared transaction amount (the bill's frozen rate is read from its posted AP-control journal line, not re-looked-up), posted to the `fx_realized_gain`/`fx_realized_loss` posting-default account inside the SAME payment entry. This required a behaviour-preserving extension to `service/journal.post_entry`: a new keyword `skip_translation: bool = False` — when the caller has already set explicit per-line functional amounts (the only case where functional ≠ transaction × a single entry rate), the engine validates those balance instead of re-translating. The realized-FX line is denominated in the functional currency and carries a positive transaction amount equal to its functional amount, so the per-line one-side CHECK (D-017, on transaction amounts) holds while the balance trigger (functional sums only) balances — no zero/zero line. Open items are partner-keyed by the opaque `partner_id` stamped on the AP control line (D-029); finance imports no module above it (verified). AP documents register in `core_documents` and link bill→journal (`posts`) and payment→bills (`pays`) so the document-flow chain spans the AP flow. Migration `0012_finance_ap` creates four tables and alters nothing (no trigger-bearing table touched, D-022); autogenerate confirms zero model drift on SQLite.
42:- **D-037 Inventory costing (PLAN 5.3): valuation is per (item, warehouse); the move ledger + quants are the quantity SSOT, valuation/layers are the value SSOT, all updated in ONE transaction; COGS posts via the event bus in that same transaction:** Which engine a `(item, warehouse)` uses is the item's `costing_method` (MOVING_AVERAGE | FIFO), defaulted from its category. **Moving average** — `inv_item_valuations` (UNIQUE(tenant,item,warehouse), `CHECK(on_hand_qty >= 0)`) holds `on_hand_qty`, full-precision `avg_unit_cost`, `total_value`, locked `with_for_update` (PG row lock; SQLite FOR-UPDATE no-op + single-writer lock, D-020): receipt adds `qty×unit_cost` and recomputes `avg = total_value/on_hand` **unrounded**; issue subtracts `quantize(qty×avg, currency dp, HALF_UP)` and, when on_hand hits **exactly 0**, **flushes the residual `total_value` to the price-difference account** so value and quantity never disagree (the rounding-drift absorber — value lands at exactly 0 even for non-terminating averages). **FIFO** — `inv_cost_layers` (one per receipt, `CHECK(0 <= remaining_qty <= original_qty)`) consumed oldest-first by `(received_at, created_at, id)` under `with_for_update` (created_at is the insertion-order tiebreaker when dates tie — uuid4 ids are not monotonic), with one `inv_layer_consumptions` row per touched layer (the per-layer COGS audit trail AND the **exact-reversal** record). **Cost input:** `inv_stock_moves.unit_cost` (MoneyType nullable, batch-added) — RECEIPT/positive-ADJUSTMENT REQUIRE it (the entry cost); ISSUE/negative-ADJUSTMENT IGNORE it and the engine computes/writes it back; TRANSFER carries the current valuation. **Same-transaction COGS (the inventory↔finance seam, D-011/D-020):** `create_move` updates valuation/layers right after the quant update, then `publish(StockValued(...))` (buffered) carrying the value Δ, the three GL account ids (inventory/COGS/price-difference, opaque per D-029) AND the **chosen offset account** (ISSUE→COGS, RECEIPT/ADJUSTMENT→price-difference, reversal→the opposite of the original's offset); `run_in_uow` drains it before commit and `finance/handlers.py` (the **first real cross-module handler**) posts the journal **through the finance posting service** (`create_draft_entry` + `post_entry`, never raw inserts) in the shared session — so one commit = move + quant + valuation + journal + docflow `posts` link, and **any handler failure rolls the whole transaction back** (a stock move can never exist without its journal entry). The COGS journal posts with `move_date`, so a move dated into a **closed period** fails (the period trigger fires in the same transaction → the move rolls back; you cannot move stock into a closed period — correct by construction). **Postings:** RECEIPT/ADJUSTMENT-up Dr inventory / Cr price-difference (standalone offset; procurement GR overrides later, 6.x); ISSUE Dr COGS / Cr inventory; ADJUSTMENT-down Dr price-difference / Cr inventory; **TRANSFER within one inventory account is value-neutral → NO event, NO journal**; a reversal posts the exact reverse of the original's entry. **Reversal is replay, not recompute:** reversing an ISSUE replays its consumptions backward onto the exact layers / re-adds MAV value at the original cost; reversing a RECEIPT zeros its layer (only if unconsumed, else error) / removes MAV value. **Read surface:** `GET /stock-valuations` + `GET /items/{id}/cost-layers` (permission `inventory.valuation.read`); `queries.item_value`/`valuation_summary` for the inventory-value KPI sum qty×cost in **Python** (typed Decimals), never `func.sum(qty×cost)` — two scaled-integer columns multiply to ×10^12 on SQLite which MoneyType cannot un-scale (D-015 discipline). **Structure:** costing service split into `costing.py` (orchestration), `costing_mav.py`, `costing_fifo.py`, `costing_reversal.py` (all <400 lines); handler registered at the app factory `register_event_handlers` (the deterministic D-011 seam, re-runnable + idempotent so the test harness re-registers after `clear_subscriptions`). Migration `0022_inventory_costing` creates three tables + batch-adds `unit_cost` to non-trigger-bearing `inv_stock_moves`, reversible, zero autogen drift; the `CHECK`s + `with_for_update` proven on real Postgres by the `-m pg` guard tests.
45:- **D-039 Vendor master (PLAN 6.1) opens procurement, owns the entity finance AP refers to by opaque id, and models payment terms as a net-days integer:** Procurement is the third business module and is placed ABOVE inventory in the dependency order — it may import `finance/queries` AND `inventory/queries` downward, and exposes its own `procurement/queries.py` as the only file modules above it import (STRUCTURE §5). **(a) The vendor IS finance AP's `partner_id` (D-029 made concrete).** Finance owns no vendor table; every AP bill/payment already stores its vendor as an opaque `partner_id` (a plain `Uuid`, no FK) + a denormalized `partner_name`. PLAN 6.1 makes `Vendor.id` exactly that `partner_id`: procurement owns the entity, finance refers to it by opaque id, and `queries.get_vendor_for_partner` resolves a bill's `partner_id` back to a vendor for AP aging/reporting. Finance can never FK to `proc_vendors` (it is below procurement) — the relationship is by id only, the inventory-item/GL-account precedent. **(b) Payment terms = a `payment_terms_days` integer on the vendor, not a terms master.** A net-days value (30 = NET30, CHECK ≥0, default 30) drives AP due dates as `bill_date + days` — the simplest model that matches how AP already computes them. Richer term schedules (2/10 NET30 early-payment discounts, multi-instalment plans) are deferred per the s4hana-parity Procurement section and would arrive as a separate terms entity referenced from the vendor; the integer is forward-compatible. **(c) Vendor codes are user-supplied, unique per tenant, no auto-sequence** (the item_code/account-code precedent — a master carries a code, not a gapless document number; the P2P documents in 6.2+ claim gapless numbers, the master does not). **(d) Approved items are an info-record-lite.** `proc_vendor_approved_items` captures the vendor↔item link (with the vendor's own SKU) but NO time-dependent price/lead-time/valid-from-to — exactly the parity "purchasing info records = PARTIAL" cut. The `item_id` is an OPAQUE inventory id (validated via `inventory/queries.item_exists`, no cross-module FK, D-029), while `vendor_id` is an intra-module composite tenant_fk. **(e) Vendor status (ACTIVE/BLOCKED/INACTIVE) has no terminal state** — all three transitions are allowed, because a block/retire must be reversible and a vendor's AP history must stay referenceable; 6.2 reads the status to refuse new POs against non-ACTIVE vendors (a soft policy at the chain, not a master-level lock). **(f) Sanctioned cross-module query added:** `finance/queries.currency_exists` (the by-code existence check the vendor's `default_currency_code` validates against, mirroring `account_exists`); inventory/queries needed nothing new. No events/handlers ship in 6.1 — vendor master drives no cross-module effects; those arrive with the P2P documents in 6.2+.
46:- **D-040 Procurement P2P chain (PLAN 6.2): requisition → RFQ → PO numbered at CREATION, gated by a single-characteristic value-threshold rule, with approved-items ENFORCED on POs:** The three procurement documents (`PurchaseRequisition`/`PurchaseRequisitionLine`, `Rfq`/`RfqLine`, `PurchaseOrder`/`PurchaseOrderLine`) are each `DocumentMixin` header+line pairs registered in `core_documents` with predecessor/successor docflow edges (`"sourced_by"` requisition→rfq, `"ordered_by"` rfq→po and requisition→po). **(a) Numbering claimed AT CREATION, not posting.** Unlike finance (which numbers a bill/journal at *posting*), procurement claims the gapless `PR-`/`RFQ-`/`PO-` number when the document is *created* — a DRAFT requisition already prints a number the sourcing/ordering chain quotes, so the document is referenceable immediately (the orders/receipts claim-timing branch of D-012, the inventory stock-move precedent). Gaplessness still holds: creation IS the committing transaction, so the counter increment and the row insert commit-or-roll-back together. **(b) The approval rule is data-driven, single-characteristic (amount), single-step, single-currency** (`proc_approval_rules`, UNIQUE(tenant, document_type ∈ {REQUISITION, PURCHASE_ORDER}), `threshold_amount` CHECK ≥0). `service.requires_approval(document_type, amount, currency)` returns True iff `amount >= threshold` AND the rule's currency matches the document's; **no active rule, an inactive rule, or a currency mismatch ⇒ no gate** (a tenant that hasn't configured thresholds runs without approval; cross-currency thresholds need FX, deferred). This is exactly the parity "approval/release strategies = PARTIAL, data-driven value-threshold rules only" cut — multi-characteristic / multi-step release strategies are the documented later. The submit step (requisition, on the estimated total) and the send step (PO, on `total_amount`) consult it: at/above ⇒ stay SUBMITTED / go PENDING_APPROVAL awaiting the distinct `.approve` key; below ⇒ auto-approve. **(c) Approved-items are ENFORCED on POs, not advisory.** A PO line item MUST be in the vendor's approved-items list (an inactive approval counts as not approved) else 422 `procurement.item_not_approved`; the vendor must be ACTIVE else 422 `procurement.vendor_not_active` — the v1 source-control rule, read through `procurement/queries` (never a cross-module FK). **(d) An RFQ targets ONE vendor in v1** (multi-bidder comparison deferred); a PO **snapshots** the vendor's `payment_terms_days` + currency at create so a later vendor edit cannot rewrite an open PO's due-date math (the 6.4 bill reads the snapshot). **(e) PO line columns staged for 6.3/6.4 now:** `received_quantity` (default 0, raised by 6.3 goods receipts; `po_line_open_quantity` = ordered − received) and the opaque `tax_code_id` (for the 6.4 bill) land in the 6.2 schema so GR + match need no migration. **(f) NO events in 6.2** — nothing in the chain posts to finance/inventory (a PO is a commitment, not a posting); the first procurement event is the 6.3 goods receipt (→ inventory move + GR/IR journal), so `events.py`/`handlers.py` stay absent (no-stub rule). **(g) Behaviour-preserving package splits** at the 400-line cap (the finance/inventory precedent, re-exported so import sites are unchanged): `models/`, `schemas/`, `service/` packages + sibling `requisition_router`/`rfq_router`/`po_router`/`approval_rule_router` mounted into `router.py`. Migration `0025_procurement_documents` creates seven tables + indexes, no trigger-bearing alters, reversible, portable both engines (zero autogen drift, applies on PG to head).
47:- **D-041 Procurement goods receipt (PLAN 6.3): a GR posts via the event bus into inventory (Dr Inventory / Cr GR-IR) using the inventory valuation-offset override; the GR↔move link is docflow, not a cross-module FK; the whole chain (GR + moves + journals + PO update) is one atomic transaction:** A `GoodsReceipt`/`GoodsReceiptLine` (`proc_goods_receipts`/`_lines`, `DocumentMixin` + gapless `GR-` number claimed at creation, `purchase_order_id` composite FK, `vendor_id` + per-line `item_id`/`unit_cost` snapshot from the PO line, opaque `warehouse_id`/`bin_id` validated via `inventory/queries`) records receipt of PO goods. **Lifecycle DRAFT → POSTED** (chosen over post-at-creation): a GR is a document a clerk builds line-by-line then posts, unlike a stock move which is permanent at creation; DRAFT can CANCEL, **POSTED is terminal** (corrected by a reversing GR / return — Phase 7 RMA; v1 ships no reverse-GR). **(a) The GR/IR three-way flow.** Posting a GR posts **Dr Inventory / Cr GR-IR clearing** (`gr_ir_clearing` is a new per-tenant posting default — a LIABILITY/clearing account; `finance/queries.gr_ir_clearing_account` resolves it and raises 422 `finance.posting_default_unmapped` when unmapped, so a GR can't post without it). The 6.4 bill posts Dr GR-IR / Cr AP, clearing it — GR/IR holds received-not-invoiced value. **(b) The valuation-offset override (the inventory integration point).** `inventory/service/stock_moves.create_move` gains an optional `valuation_offset_account_id`; for a RECEIPT it OVERRIDES the costing engine's standard price-difference offset — the engine sets `StockValued.offset_account_id` to it and `finance/handlers.post_stock_valuation_journal` (already generic over the offset) credits GR/IR instead. The override threads end-to-end `create_move → costing.apply_costing → _apply_inbound → StockValued.offset_account_id → finance/handlers`, changes only the Cr leg never the costing math, is ignored on non-receipt types and on reversals, and defaults None ⇒ the standalone-receipt behaviour (and its tests) is unchanged. **(c) The cross-module mechanism is the EVENT BUS, not a direct call (the STRUCTURE §5 crux).** Procurement must NOT import inventory's service (modules never import each other's service.py/models.py). So `post_goods_receipt` publishes `procurement/events.GoodsReceiptPosted` (a plain typed event carrying the per-line receipts — item/bin/qty/unit_cost/lot/serial/inspection — plus the resolved GR/IR account, move_date, and the GR document id), and **`inventory/handlers.py`** (new — the first inventory handler) subscribes and calls its OWN `stock_moves.create_move` per line with `valuation_offset_account_id`=GR/IR. Those moves in turn publish `StockValued`, which finance handles — a **two-hop, same-transaction chain** (procurement → inventory → finance), the exact mirror of the existing inventory→finance COGS pattern (publisher exposes events; subscriber's handlers.py imports the publisher's events.py + the link-type constant, the sanctioned §5 events allowance — finance/handlers importing inventory.constants is the precedent). Verified: `grep` confirms procurement imports ONLY `finance/queries` + `inventory/queries` (no service/models); inventory/handlers imports only procurement `events` + the `moved_by` link constant. **(d) The GR↔move linkage is DOCFLOW, not a cross-module FK.** Inventory owns the move, so a GR line carries NO `stock_move_id` column; instead the handler writes a docflow edge GR→`moved_by`→move (and procurement writes PO→`received_by`→GR), so the chain is queryable without procurement FK-ing into inventory's table. **(e) The whole post is ONE atomic transaction** in `run_in_uow`: GR status + `posted_at` + the PO `received_quantity` raise + PO status advance (PARTIALLY_RECEIVED if any line open, RECEIVED if all fully received) are procurement's own writes; the N moves + N inventory-debit/GR-IR journals are the handler's; all commit together or roll back together. A **closed-period `receipt_date`** trips a move's journal period trigger inside the same transaction and rolls the **entire** post back (no move, no journal, GR stays DRAFT, PO untouched) — correct by construction. **(f) Over-receipt is REJECTED in v1** (422 `procurement.over_receipt`) — a receipt line cannot exceed its PO line's open quantity (ordered − received); a configurable tolerance is a 6.4/later refinement. The PO must be APPROVED/SENT/PARTIALLY_RECEIVED to receive (else 422 `procurement.po_not_receivable`). **(g) The inspection hook is a FLAG ONLY in v1.** `requires_inspection` (per GR line, default False) flags the received line and is passed through to the stock move for traceability — it does NOT route to a QI bin, block downstream use, or gate the move; the inspection-lot disposition (accept/reject/rework) is Phase 9 Quality. **(h) Inline, no background path** — a GR is a single delivery (small), so the post runs inline (O(lines)), unlike bulk count posts / payment runs. **Structure:** writes (`service/goods_receipts.py`, 373 lines) split from reads (`service/goods_receipt_reads.py`) at the cap; `models/goods_receipts.py` + `schemas/goods_receipts.py` re-exported from the packages; sibling `goods_receipt_router.py` mounted into `router.py` (the one-surface precedent); `inventory/service/stock_moves.py` re-trimmed to 399 lines after the override param. Migration `0026_procurement_goods_receipts` creates two tables + indexes, NO trigger-bearing alters (the `gr_ir_clearing` purpose is data, the valuation-offset is a service param — neither is schema), reversible, portable both engines, applies on PG to head.

143	      period or insufficient handler rolls it ALL back). TERMINAL: a POSTED GR is corrected by a

1	"""Procurement's cross-module read interface (STRUCTURE §5).
2	
3	Procurement sits above inventory (and finance) in the dependency order: the P2P documents in
4	6.2–6.4 (requisition → RFQ → PO → goods receipt → 3-way match) and finance AP reporting read THIS
5	file to resolve vendor state synchronously; procurement imports finance/queries + inventory/queries
6	downward. Keep this surface thin and stable — it is a contract; it is the ONLY procurement file
7	other modules import.
8	
9	The central D-029 link: finance AP stores a vendor on each bill/payment as an opaque ``partner_id``
10	(no FK). ``get_vendor_for_partner`` resolves that ``partner_id`` back to a ``Vendor`` so AP aging /
11	reporting can render the vendor's name and payment terms — the ``partner_id`` IS the ``Vendor.id``,
12	so it is a thin alias over ``get_vendor`` named for the reporting intent.
13	
14	PLAN 6.2 adds the PURCHASE-ORDER reads 6.3 (goods receipts) and 6.4 (the 3-way match) call:
15	``get_purchase_order``, ``po_line_open_quantity`` (ordered − received), ``get_po_for_receipt`` (the
16	header + lines a receipt needs) and ``open_po_lines_for_vendor`` (the awaiting-receipt worklist).
17	
18	Every function takes an explicit ``tenant_id`` and runs under the caller's tenant context, so the
19	D-007 filter applies on top of the explicit predicate — ordinary tenant-scoped reads, not a bypass.
20	"""
21	
22	import uuid
23	from decimal import Decimal
24	
25	from sqlalchemy import select
26	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
27	
28	from app.modules.procurement.constants import PurchaseOrderStatus
29	from app.modules.procurement.models import (
30	    GoodsReceipt,
31	    PurchaseOrder,
32	    PurchaseOrderLine,
33	    Vendor,
34	    VendorApprovedItem,
35	)
36	
37	
38	async def get_vendor(
39	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, vendor_id: uuid.UUID
40	) -> Vendor | None:
41	    """The vendor with ``vendor_id`` in the tenant, or None. Lets another module read a vendor's
42	    master fields (name, status, default currency, payment terms) without importing procurement
43	    models directly — the analogue of inventory's ``get_item``."""
44	    stmt = select(Vendor).where(Vendor.tenant_id == tenant_id, Vendor.id == vendor_id)
45	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
46	
47	
48	async def get_vendor_for_partner(
49	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, partner_id: uuid.UUID
50	) -> Vendor | None:
51	    """The vendor an AP document's opaque ``partner_id`` refers to (D-029), or None. AP aging /
52	    reporting calls this to resolve a bill's ``partner_id`` to a vendor name + payment terms. The
53	    ``partner_id`` IS the ``Vendor.id`` (finance stores it without an FK), so this is ``get_vendor``
54	    named for the reporting intent — kept as its own function so AP call sites read intent-first and
55	    the alias survives any future indirection."""
56	    return await get_vendor(session, tenant_id, partner_id)
57	
58	
59	async def vendor_exists(
60	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, vendor_id: uuid.UUID
61	) -> bool:
62	    """Whether a vendor with ``vendor_id`` exists in the tenant. The cheap existence check a
63	    requisition / PO line uses to validate its vendor_id (the procurement analogue of inventory's
64	    ``item_exists``)."""
65	    stmt = select(Vendor.id).where(Vendor.tenant_id == tenant_id, Vendor.id == vendor_id)
66	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).first() is not None
67	
68	
69	async def vendor_payment_terms_days(
70	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, vendor_id: uuid.UUID
71	) -> int | None:
72	    """The vendor's net-days payment terms (e.g. 30 = NET30), or None if the vendor does not exist.
73	    The PO→bill flow (6.4) reads this to default a bill's due date (bill_date + days), the same
74	    math AP uses today — exposed so the chain need not import procurement models."""
75	    stmt = select(Vendor.payment_terms_days).where(
76	        Vendor.tenant_id == tenant_id, Vendor.id == vendor_id
77	    )
78	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()

81	async def vendor_default_currency(
82	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, vendor_id: uuid.UUID
83	) -> str | None:
84	    """The vendor's default currency code (ISO alpha-3), or None if the vendor does not exist. The
85	    PO flow (6.2) defaults a PO's currency from this; exposed so the chain need not import
86	    procurement models."""
87	    stmt = select(Vendor.default_currency_code).where(
88	        Vendor.tenant_id == tenant_id, Vendor.id == vendor_id
89	    )
90	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
91	
92	
93	async def is_item_approved_for_vendor(
94	    session: AsyncSession,
95	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
96	    vendor_id: uuid.UUID,
97	    item_id: uuid.UUID,
98	) -> bool:
99	    """Whether ``item_id`` is an ACTIVE approved item for ``vendor_id`` (PLAN 6.1, the
100	    info-record-lite).
101	    The PO flow (6.2) calls this to enforce "only approved sources" when a tenant opts into it (a
102	    soft policy hook); an inactive approval reads False so a deactivated source is treated as not
103	    approved. Index-served by ``(tenant_id, vendor_id)``."""
104	    stmt = select(VendorApprovedItem.id).where(
105	        VendorApprovedItem.tenant_id == tenant_id,
106	        VendorApprovedItem.vendor_id == vendor_id,
107	        VendorApprovedItem.item_id == item_id,
108	        VendorApprovedItem.is_active.is_(True),
109	    )
110	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).first() is not None
111	
112	
113	# --- Purchase orders (PLAN 6.2 → consumed by 6.3 goods receipts + 6.4 3-way match) ------------
114	
115	
116	async def get_purchase_order(
117	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, po_id: uuid.UUID
118	) -> PurchaseOrder | None:
119	    """The PO with ``po_id`` in the tenant, or None. Lets 6.3 (goods receipts) and 6.4 (the bill
120	    match) read a PO header — vendor, currency, status, totals — without importing procurement
121	    service internals. A point lookup on the PK."""
122	    stmt = select(PurchaseOrder).where(
123	        PurchaseOrder.tenant_id == tenant_id, PurchaseOrder.id == po_id
124	    )
125	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
126	
127	
128	async def po_line_open_quantity(
129	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, po_line_id: uuid.UUID
130	) -> Decimal | None:
131	    """The still-open quantity on a PO line — ordered minus received — or None if the line does not
132	    exist. 6.3 reads this to cap a goods receipt at the outstanding quantity; 6.4 reads it for the
133	    three-way match. Computed from the maintained ``received_quantity`` (raised by 6.3), so it is a
134	    point lookup, not a SUM over receipts."""
135	    line = (
136	        await session.execute(
137	            select(PurchaseOrderLine).where(
138	                PurchaseOrderLine.tenant_id == tenant_id,
139	                PurchaseOrderLine.id == po_line_id,
140	            )
141	        )
142	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
143	    if line is None:
144	        return None
145	    return Decimal(str(line.quantity)) - Decimal(str(line.received_quantity))
146	
147	
148	async def get_po_for_receipt(
149	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, po_id: uuid.UUID
150	) -> tuple[PurchaseOrder, list[PurchaseOrderLine]] | None:
151	    """The PO header + its lines (item, ordered/received quantities, unit cost, tax code) — the data
152	    a goods receipt (6.3) needs to build receipt lines and a 3-way match (6.4) needs to compare.
153	    None when the PO is unknown to this tenant. Two indexed reads (header by PK, lines by
154	    (tenant, po_id)); no N+1 over lines."""
155	    po = await get_purchase_order(session, tenant_id, po_id)
156	    if po is None:
157	        return None
158	    lines = list(
159	        (
160	            await session.execute(
161	                select(PurchaseOrderLine)
162	                .where(
163	                    PurchaseOrderLine.tenant_id == tenant_id,
164	                    PurchaseOrderLine.po_id == po_id,
165	                )
166	                .order_by(PurchaseOrderLine.line_number)
167	            )
168	        )
169	        .scalars()
170	        .all()
171	    )
172	    return po, lines
173	
174	
175	async def get_goods_receipt(
176	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, gr_id: uuid.UUID
177	) -> GoodsReceipt | None:
178	    """The goods receipt with ``gr_id`` in the tenant, or None (PLAN 6.3). Lets 6.4 (the bill match)
179	    read a GR header — PO, vendor, status, receipt date — without importing procurement service
180	    internals. A point lookup on the PK."""
181	    stmt = select(GoodsReceipt).where(
182	        GoodsReceipt.tenant_id == tenant_id, GoodsReceipt.id == gr_id
183	    )
184	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
185	
186	
187	async def goods_receipts_for_po(
188	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, po_id: uuid.UUID
189	) -> list[GoodsReceipt]:
190	    """Every goods receipt raised against a PO (PLAN 6.3), newest first — the per-PO receipt history
191	    the 6.4 three-way match reads to find what has been received. Index-served by
192	    (tenant, purchase_order_id)."""
193	    stmt = (
194	        select(GoodsReceipt)
195	        .where(
196	            GoodsReceipt.tenant_id == tenant_id,
197	            GoodsReceipt.purchase_order_id == po_id,
198	        )
199	        .order_by(GoodsReceipt.created_at.desc())
200	    )
201	    return list((await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all())
202	
203	
204	async def open_po_lines_for_vendor(
205	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, vendor_id: uuid.UUID
206	) -> list[PurchaseOrderLine]:
207	    """The still-open PO lines (ordered > received) on SENT / PARTIALLY_RECEIVED orders for a vendor
208	    — the receivable-against-vendor worklist 6.3 / 6.4 use to find what is awaiting receipt. Filters
209	    on the (tenant, vendor_id, status) index; the open-quantity test is a column comparison."""
210	    stmt = (
211	        select(PurchaseOrderLine)
212	        .join(
213	            PurchaseOrder,
214	            (PurchaseOrderLine.tenant_id == PurchaseOrder.tenant_id)
215	            & (PurchaseOrderLine.po_id == PurchaseOrder.id),
216	        )
217	        .where(
218	            PurchaseOrder.tenant_id == tenant_id,
219	            PurchaseOrder.vendor_id == vendor_id,
220	            PurchaseOrder.status.in_(
221	                [
222	                    PurchaseOrderStatus.SENT.value,
223	                    PurchaseOrderStatus.PARTIALLY_RECEIVED.value,
224	                ]
225	            ),
226	            PurchaseOrderLine.received_quantity < PurchaseOrderLine.quantity,
227	        )
228	        .order_by(PurchaseOrder.created_at, PurchaseOrderLine.line_number)
229	    )
230	    return list((await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all())

1	"""Vendor-bill lifecycle: draft creation + posting through the journal (PLAN 4.5, AP).
2	
3	A vendor bill is the AP-side document. ``create_vendor_bill`` computes input tax (via the shared
4	tax engine) and totals on a DRAFT; ``post_vendor_bill`` builds and posts the AP journal entry
5	(Dr each expense/asset line net, Dr input tax to the tax code's receivable account, Cr the AP
6	control for the gross — with the opaque ``partner_id`` stamped on the AP line, D-029), claims the
7	gapless system number (D-012), links the bill document to its journal entry (docflow), sets
8	``open_amount`` = gross, and publishes ``VendorBillPosted``. Idempotent at the service level: a
9	re-post of an already-POSTED bill returns it unchanged.
10	
11	The journal engine handles FX translation at posting (D-019): a foreign-currency bill's functional
12	amounts are frozen at the posting-date SPOT rate by the same machinery every entry uses. Finance
13	stays the bottom dependency — this module imports no other module.
14	"""

108	async def create_vendor_bill(
109	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, payload: VendorBillCreate
110	) -> VendorBill:
111	    """Create a DRAFT vendor bill + lines (PLAN 4.5). Validates the AP control + every line account
112	    exists; computes input tax per line via the shared tax engine (so net/tax/gross match Sales/AR)
113	    and rolls up the bill totals. Registers the document in core_documents with NO number (claimed
114	    at posting, D-012). ``open_amount`` stays 0 until posting. Does NOT post a journal entry."""
115	    if not payload.lines:
116	        raise ValidationFailedError(
117	            message="A vendor bill needs at least one line",
118	            code="finance.vendor_bill_no_lines",
119	        )
120	    await _require_account(session, tenant_id, payload.ap_account_id, label="AP control")
121	
122	    gross_total = Decimal(0)
123	    tax_total = Decimal(0)
124	    net_total = Decimal(0)
125	    line_rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
126	    for index, line in enumerate(payload.lines, start=1):
127	        await _require_account(session, tenant_id, line.account_id, label="line")
128	        net = quantize_for_currency(line.net_amount, payload.currency_code)
129	        tax_amount = Decimal(0)
130	        if line.tax_code_id is not None:
131	            tax_code = await _tax_code(session, tenant_id, line.tax_code_id)
132	            calc = calculate_line_tax(
133	                net, tax_code, direction=TaxDirection.INPUT, currency_code=payload.currency_code
134	            )
135	            net = calc.net_amount
136	            tax_amount = calc.tax_amount
137	        net_total += net
138	        tax_total += tax_amount
139	        gross_total += net + tax_amount
140	        line_rows.append(
141	            {
142	                "line_number": index,
143	                "account_id": line.account_id,
144	                "description": line.description,
145	                "net_amount": net,
146	                "tax_code_id": line.tax_code_id,
147	                "tax_amount": tax_amount,
148	                "cost_center_id": line.cost_center_id,
149	                "project_id": line.project_id,
150	            }
151	        )
152	
153	    bill_id = uuid.uuid4()
154	    document = await docflow.register_document(
155	        session,
156	        tenant_id,
157	        AP_BILL_DOC_TYPE,
158	        bill_id,
159	        doc_number=None,
160	        status=BillStatus.DRAFT.value,
161	    )
162	    bill = VendorBill(
163	        id=bill_id,
164	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
165	        document_id=document.id,
166	        partner_id=payload.partner_id,
167	        partner_name=payload.partner_name,
168	        bill_external_ref=payload.bill_external_ref,
169	        bill_date=payload.bill_date,
170	        due_date=payload.due_date,
171	        currency_code=payload.currency_code,
172	        status=BillStatus.DRAFT.value,
173	        ap_account_id=payload.ap_account_id,
174	        gross_amount=gross_total,
175	        tax_amount=tax_total,
176	        net_amount=net_total,
177	        open_amount=Decimal(0),
178	        description=payload.description,
179	    )
180	    session.add(bill)
181	    for row in line_rows:
182	        session.add(VendorBillLine(tenant_id=tenant_id, bill_id=bill_id, **row))
183	    await session.flush()
184	    return bill

187	def _bill_journal_lines(
188	    bill: VendorBill, lines: list[VendorBillLine], tax_account_by_code: dict[uuid.UUID, uuid.UUID]
189	) -> list[JournalLineCreate]:
190	    """The balanced AP journal lines for a bill (PLAN 4.5): Dr each line's net to its expense/asset
191	    account, Dr input tax to the tax code's receivable account (one line per line with tax), Cr the
192	    AP control for the gross — partner_id stamped on the AP line so the open item is partner-keyed
193	    (D-029). Dimensions ride to the journal line so CO projections see them."""
194	    journal_lines: list[JournalLineCreate] = []
195	    for line in lines:
196	        journal_lines.append(
197	            JournalLineCreate(
198	                account_id=line.account_id,
199	                description=line.description,
200	                transaction_debit_amount=line.net_amount,
201	                cost_center_id=line.cost_center_id,
202	                project_id=line.project_id,
203	            )
204	        )
205	        if line.tax_amount and line.tax_code_id is not None:
206	            journal_lines.append(
207	                JournalLineCreate(
208	                    account_id=tax_account_by_code[line.tax_code_id],
209	                    description="Input tax",
210	                    transaction_debit_amount=line.tax_amount,
211	                )
212	            )
213	    journal_lines.append(
214	        JournalLineCreate(
215	            account_id=bill.ap_account_id,
216	            description=f"AP {bill.partner_name}",
217	            transaction_credit_amount=bill.gross_amount,
218	            partner_type=AP_PARTNER_TYPE,
219	            partner_id=bill.partner_id,
220	        )
221	    )
222	    return journal_lines

225	async def _resolve_tax_accounts(
226	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, lines: list[VendorBillLine]
227	) -> dict[uuid.UUID, uuid.UUID]:
228	    """Map each line's tax_code_id -> its receivable (INPUT) account (PLAN 4.5). Raises a clear 422
229	    if a code that levied tax has no receivable account wired (the tax engine would otherwise post
230	    to None)."""
231	    accounts: dict[uuid.UUID, uuid.UUID] = {}
232	    for line in lines:
233	        if not line.tax_amount or line.tax_code_id is None or line.tax_code_id in accounts:
234	            continue
235	        tax_code = await _tax_code(session, tenant_id, line.tax_code_id)
236	        if tax_code.tax_receivable_account_id is None:
237	            raise ValidationFailedError(
238	                message=f"Tax code {tax_code.code} has no input-tax (receivable) account",
239	                code="finance.ap_tax_account_unwired",
240	                details={"tax_code_id": str(line.tax_code_id)},
241	            )
242	        accounts[line.tax_code_id] = tax_code.tax_receivable_account_id
243	    return accounts

246	async def post_vendor_bill(
247	    session: AsyncSession,
248	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
249	    bill_id: uuid.UUID,
250	    *,
251	    posting_date: date | None = None,
252	) -> VendorBill:
253	    """Post a DRAFT vendor bill to the journal (PLAN 4.5). Idempotent: an already-POSTED bill is
254	    returned unchanged. Builds the balanced AP entry (document_type AP_BILL), posts it via the
255	    journal engine (which claims the entry number, resolves the period, and translates FX at the
256	    posting rate, D-019), claims the bill's gapless system number, links bill->journal (docflow
257	    'posts'), sets ``open_amount`` = gross + status POSTED, and publishes ``VendorBillPosted``.
258	    ``posting_date`` defaults to the bill date."""
259	    bill = await get_vendor_bill(session, tenant_id, bill_id)
260	    if bill.status == BillStatus.POSTED.value:
261	        return bill
262	    if bill.status != BillStatus.DRAFT.value:
263	        raise ConflictError(
264	            message="Only a draft vendor bill can be posted",
265	            code="finance.vendor_bill_not_draft",
266	            details={"status": bill.status},
267	        )
268	
269	    lines = await get_vendor_bill_lines(session, tenant_id, bill_id)
270	    tax_account_by_code = await _resolve_tax_accounts(session, tenant_id, lines)
271	
272	    entry = await create_draft_entry(
273	        session,
274	        tenant_id,
275	        JournalEntryCreate(
276	            posting_date=posting_date or bill.bill_date,
277	            currency_code=bill.currency_code,
278	            description=f"Vendor bill {bill.partner_name}",
279	            document_type=DocumentType.AP_INVOICE,
280	            lines=_bill_journal_lines(bill, lines, tax_account_by_code),
281	        ),
282	    )
283	    await post_entry(session, tenant_id, entry.id)
284	
285	    await ensure_sequence(
286	        session,
287	        tenant_id,
288	        AP_BILL_SEQUENCE_NAME,
289	        AP_BILL_NUMBER_PREFIX,
290	        AP_BILL_NUMBER_PADDING,
291	        year_reset=True,
292	    )
293	    bill_number = await claim_number(
294	        session, tenant_id, AP_BILL_SEQUENCE_NAME, on_date=bill.bill_date
295	    )
296	
297	    bill.bill_number = bill_number
298	    bill.journal_entry_id = entry.id
299	    bill.open_amount = bill.gross_amount
300	    bill.status = BillStatus.POSTED.value
301	    await session.flush()
302	
303	    await docflow.set_document_status(
304	        session, tenant_id, bill.document_id, status=BillStatus.POSTED.value, doc_number=bill_number
305	    )
306	    await docflow.link_documents(
307	        session,
308	        tenant_id,
309	        predecessor=bill.document_id,
310	        successor=entry.document_id,
311	        link_type=AP_BILL_POSTS_LINK,
312	    )
313	
314	    publish(
315	        session,
316	        VendorBillPosted(
317	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
318	            bill_id=bill.id,
319	            bill_number=bill_number,
320	            journal_entry_id=entry.id,
321	            partner_id=bill.partner_id,
322	            currency_code=bill.currency_code,
323	            gross_amount=bill.gross_amount,
324	            tax_amount=bill.tax_amount,
325	            net_amount=bill.net_amount,
326	        ),
327	    )
328	    return bill

1	"""Finance domain-event handlers (D-011) — the FIRST real cross-module handler (PLAN 5.3, D-020).
2	
3	Subscribes to ``inventory.stock.valued`` and posts the COGS/inventory valuation journal in the SAME
4	transaction as the stock move (D-011 run_in_uow drains before commit; D-020 same-transaction COGS).
5	Because the handler shares the session and any handler exception rolls the WHOLE transaction back, a
6	stock move can never commit without its journal entry, or vice versa — the load-bearing atomicity
7	invariant. The journal posts with the move's ``move_date``: a date in a CLOSED period makes the
8	journal's period trigger fire inside this same transaction, which rolls the whole move back (you
9	cannot move stock into a closed accounting period — correct by construction).
10	
11	Postings per move type (the GL effect of each — D-020). The costing engine pre-selects the OFFSET
12	account per type and the event carries it, so the handler is a thin Dr/Cr direction switch:
13	- RECEIPT / ADJUSTMENT-up: Dr inventory / Cr price-difference. A STANDALONE receipt (opening
14	  balance, manual stock-in) has no procurement GR clearing yet, so its offset is price-difference /
15	  inventory-adjustment account; procurement's goods-receipt path (6.x) will OVERRIDE this with its
16	  own GR/IR offset. ADJUSTMENT-up is the same shape (a stock increase with no document behind it).
17	- ISSUE: Dr COGS / Cr inventory at the computed cost (goods left for sale/production).
18	- ADJUSTMENT-down: Dr price-difference / Cr inventory (an inventory write-off, no document).
19	- The moving-average zero-quantity FLUSH posts its residual to price-difference WITHIN the issue's
20	  entry so value and quantity never disagree (D-020).
21	- A reversal posts the EXACT reverse of the original move's entry (reversing an issue credits COGS;
22	  reversing a receipt debits price-difference) — the costing engine sets the reversal's offset.
23	- TRANSFER within one inventory account: value-neutral → the inventory engine publishes NO event, so
24	  the handler never runs for it (documented; no journal).
25	
26	The journal is built through the finance posting service (``create_draft_entry`` + ``post_entry``),
27	NEVER raw inserts, so every journal invariant (balance, one-side CHECK, period, immutability,
28	numbering, audit, docflow) fires exactly as for any posting. The move's document is linked to the
29	journal entry's document ('posts' edge) so the docflow viewer shows move -> COGS entry.
30	
31	Registration: ``app.main.register_event_handlers`` subscribes ``post_stock_valuation_journal`` to
32	the
33	event key at the app factory (the deterministic D-011 registration seam), so the test harness can
34	re-register after its per-test ``clear_subscriptions`` reset (D-025) without a module re-import.
35	"""
36	
37	from __future__ import annotations
38	
39	import uuid
40	from datetime import date
41	from decimal import Decimal
42	
43	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
44	
45	from app.core import docflow
46	from app.core.money import quantize_for_currency
47	from app.modules.finance import queries as finance_queries
48	from app.modules.finance.constants import DocumentType
49	from app.modules.finance.schemas import JournalEntryCreate, JournalLineCreate
50	from app.modules.finance.service.journal import create_draft_entry, post_entry
51	from app.modules.inventory.constants import DEFAULT_COSTING_CURRENCY, STOCK_MOVE_POSTS_LINK
52	from app.modules.inventory.events import StockValued

54	# A signed posting: (account_id, amount). Positive amount => debit, negative => credit. The line
55	# builder drops zeros and splits into the journal's one-sided debit/credit lines.
56	_SignedPosting = tuple[uuid.UUID, Decimal]
